name: Product-led
coreAngle: Define the category and make the Creative OS itself the lead idea.
headline: [PRODUCT CATEGORY] FOR APPLOVIN CREATIVE
description: For [IDEAL CUSTOMER], Upscale is the [PRODUCT CATEGORY] that [PRIMARY OUTCOME] through [MECHANISM].
sectionDirections: Name the [PRODUCT CATEGORY], [IDEAL CUSTOMER], [PRIMARY OUTCOME], and [MECHANISM], then present [PRIMARY CTA] and [SECONDARY CTA].
Preview the eight Icon-style branches: [FORMATS], [STORY], [INVESTORS / ADVISORS], [PARTNER PROGRAM], [MODULES], [COMPARISON], [CUSTOMERS], and [WORKFLOW].
Show [FORMAT COUNT] approved AppLovin creative formats with [HOOK], [USE CASE], and [APPROVED ASSET] for each.
Map the exact seven-step journey from [INPUT] to [OUTPUT], including [OWNER], [TIMING], [APPROVAL], and [COMMERCIAL TRIGGER].
Define [ENTRY OFFER], [HIGH-TOUCH OFFER], and [ENTERPRISE / PARTNER OFFER] with verified scope, price, cadence, rights, and risk controls.
Support the product thesis with [CUSTOMER COUNT], [APPROVED QUOTES], [VERIFIED RESULTS], [TEST WINDOWS], and [ATTRIBUTION].
Explain [MODULE 01–04], the function of each module, the state transitions, and how they combine into one Creative OS.
Compare Upscale with [ALTERNATIVE 01–07] only across approved dimensions, verified capabilities, and current pricing.
Connect [FOUNDER HISTORY], [VERIFIED OUTCOME], and [LEARNED INSIGHT] to why this product category exists now.
List only approved [INVESTORS / ADVISORS] and explain their customer relevance, if any.
Specify [PARTNER ICP], [BOUNTY], [REV SHARE], [QUALIFICATION], [PAYOUT TRIGGER], and reusable post formats.
Use an optional self-aware Creative OS 3.0 pricing beat with [PLAYFUL PLAN 01–02], or remove it if unapproved.
Reopen the six highest-intent branches with short, product-led descriptions and exact anchor links.
Restate [PRIMARY PROMISE], [RISK REVERSAL / TIME TO VALUE], and the same two CTA paths without adding new claims.

name: Pain-led
coreAngle: Lead with the current creative bottleneck and the tradeoff the buyer wants to remove.
headline: [PRIMARY PAIN], WITHOUT [CURRENT TRADEOFF]
description: [TARGET ROLE] uses Upscale to replace [CURRENT PROCESS] with [MECHANISM], while preserving [NON-NEGOTIABLE].
sectionDirections: Frame [PRIMARY PAIN], [CURRENT PROCESS], [CURRENT TRADEOFF], [NON-NEGOTIABLE], and the two next-step CTAs.
Use the eight swipe cards to route each major pain to the relevant proof, workflow, product, or commercial section.
Organize creative formats by the pain they solve: [FATIGUE], [SPEED], [VOLUME], [LOCALIZATION], or other approved problems.
Show where the current process breaks, then map the seven-step replacement workflow with owners, timings, approvals, and handoffs.
Price the solution against [COST OF CURRENT PAIN] using only approved numbers, with clear scope, terms, and switching protections.
Select customer stories that document the same pain, baseline, intervention, test window, and verified result.
Describe how [MODULE 01–04] address the pain without claiming unsupported automation, integrations, or performance.
Compare [CURRENT PROCESS / ALTERNATIVES] across the approved pain dimensions, implementation burden, and verified cost.
Tell the founder story through the first-hand observation of [PRIMARY PAIN] and the evidence that shaped Upscale.
Use [INVESTOR / ADVISOR] proof only where it reduces a specific buyer concern or implementation risk.
Position the partner program around helping [PARTNER ICP] identify and refer teams experiencing [PRIMARY PAIN].
Use the optional pattern-break to exaggerate the old workflow’s absurdity through placeholders, subject to approval.
Reopen the pain diagnosis, customer evidence, workflow, comparison, product, and partner branches.
Close on the cost of leaving [PRIMARY PAIN] unresolved, then repeat [PRIMARY CTA] and [SECONDARY CTA].

name: Outcome-led
coreAngle: Lead with the buyer’s desired creative result and make proof architecture the central thread.
headline: [PRIMARY OUTCOME] FROM EVERY CREATIVE CYCLE
description: Turn [INPUT] into [PRIMARY OUTCOME] for AppLovin through [MECHANISM], measured by [APPROVED KPI].
sectionDirections: Define [PRIMARY OUTCOME], [INPUT], [MECHANISM], [APPROVED KPI], and the two CTA paths without implying a guarantee.
Use the eight cards to preview the evidence, workflow, formats, product, commercial model, and credibility behind the outcome.
Show which [FORMAT 01–04] are hypothesized or proven to support [PRIMARY OUTCOME], with approved evidence labels.
Map the seven-step operating rhythm and identify the KPI, decision, owner, and output at each stage.
Tie each offer to an explicit [DELIVERABLE], [MEASUREMENT PLAN], [CADENCE], [PRICE], and [RISK CONTROL].
Lead with the strongest approved customer evidence, including baseline, sample, test window, attribution, and limitations.
Explain the module chain from [INPUT] to [OUTPUT] and where [APPROVED KPI] is observed or exported.
Compare alternatives on outcome-relevant dimensions only, with current evidence and no implied superiority where data is missing.
Connect the founder’s verified experience to the pursuit of [PRIMARY OUTCOME] and the product thesis.
Show approved backers or advisors only when their expertise strengthens the outcome narrative.
Define how partners qualify, refer, and get paid for customers seeking [PRIMARY OUTCOME].
Use the optional joke-price cards as a tonal reset, keeping every price and promise as a placeholder.
Reopen proof, formats, workflow, product, comparison, and commercial branches for outcome-focused buyers.
Repeat [PRIMARY OUTCOME], the evidence qualifier, and both CTAs without introducing a new metric.

name: Workflow-led
coreAngle: Lead with the operating system and make the seven-step process the primary differentiator.
headline: FROM [INPUT] TO [OUTPUT], IN ONE CREATIVE OS
description: Bring [INPUT], [WORKFLOW], and [OUTPUT] into one creative operating layer for [TARGET TEAM].
sectionDirections: Name [INPUT], [OUTPUT], [TARGET TEAM], [WORKFLOW PROBLEM], and the two CTA paths.
Use the eight cards as an operating map that links formats, workflow, modules, proof, comparison, and commercial choices.
Define each format as a reusable workflow object with [REQUIRED INPUTS], [OWNER], [APPROVAL], and [OUTPUT].
Make the seven-step section the narrative center: exact owner, timing, system state, approval gate, billing trigger, and output per step.
Package the workflow by level of ownership: [ENTRY], [HIGH-TOUCH], and [ENTERPRISE / PARTNER], with verified terms.
Choose stories that prove workflow change using approved cycle-time, throughput, quality, or collaboration evidence.
Map [MODULE 01–04] to the seven steps and show the approved states, handoffs, and integrations for each.
Compare Upscale with [ALTERNATIVE 01–07] on workflow coverage, ownership, approvals, visibility, and verified cost.
Tell the founder story around the operational gap that led to the Creative OS model.
Use approved operator and advisor credibility where it validates workflow design or implementation experience.
Explain the referral and implementation handoff for [PARTNER ICP], including qualification and economics.
Use the optional pattern-break to contrast one operating system with [FRAGMENTED TOOL COUNT], if approved.
Reopen the workflow, modules, formats, comparison, customer, and partner branches.
Close by restating the [INPUT]-to-[OUTPUT] system and both CTAs, with the same timing and risk language.

name: Proof-led
coreAngle: Lead with the strongest verified evidence and make sourcing and qualification visible throughout.
headline: [VERIFIED PROOF POINT] FOR [TARGET SEGMENT]
description: Across [TEST WINDOW / SAMPLE], Upscale delivered [VERIFIED RESULT] for [TARGET SEGMENT], measured by [ATTRIBUTION METHOD].
sectionDirections: Lead with one fully sourced [VERIFIED PROOF POINT], [TARGET SEGMENT], [SAMPLE], [TEST WINDOW], and [ATTRIBUTION METHOD].
Route visitors from the proof claim to customers, workflow, formats, product, comparison, credibility, and commercial detail.
Show only formats with approved examples or label each item [HYPOTHESIS] until performance evidence is supplied.
Document the seven-step process that produced the proof, including inputs, owners, timing, approvals, and controls.
State offer scope and pricing separately from performance evidence; include all terms, rights, and risk language.
Expand the lead proof into attributed customer stories with sources, baselines, samples, windows, and limitations.
Show which [MODULE 01–04] were actually involved in the verified result and leave unused capabilities as placeholders.
Use evidence-backed comparison rows only; mark every unsourced competitor value [VERIFY].
Include only verified founder milestones that explain the capability to produce or measure the result.
List approved investors or advisors as named credibility, without implying endorsement of the performance claim.
Define partner claims, economics, and qualification independently from customer performance evidence.
Keep the optional pattern-break claim-free, or remove it if it weakens the proof-led tone.
Reopen customer evidence, methods, workflow, formats, product, and comparison for verification-minded buyers.
Repeat the same sourced proof point, qualifier, and two CTAs; do not introduce a second unsourced claim.
